title: The Half-Light Aftermath
premise: Quentin Eriksen, a translator whose childhood language is dissolving word by word, hears a song on the radio that exists nowhere — one her late mother composed and never recorded. The melody pulls her back to the family house days before its sale closes, where her estranged siblings have gathered to divide what remains. As Quentin pieces together who gave the song to the radio station and why, she uncovers the sacrifice her mother made that the whole family silently arranged itself around. At the closing, Quentin chooses to keep the house as a shared refuge rather than sell it, reclaiming her language and her place in a found-and-forgiven family.
about_author: Yara Fairweather is the pen name of a former court interpreter who grew up between two languages and two coastlines. She writes about the quiet violence of assimilation and the stubborn afterlives of family songs.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Working a translation job in the city, Quentin fumbles a childhood word she can no longer recall, then hears an unrecorded melody — her mother's — playing on a late-night radio program. Shaken, she calls the station and learns the tape was mailed anonymously. The beat is vertigo: the past asserting it still owns her.

chapters.title: The House Before the Sale
chapters.summary: Quentin arrives at the family house, where her brother Anders and sister Mireille are boxing up rooms with brisk, wounded efficiency. Quentin plays them the radio recording; Anders insists the song is a coincidence, Mireille goes silent. In the attic they find the reel-to-reel — and a letter addressed to all three, unopened. The beat is dread dressed as nostalgia.

chapters.title: What Mother Gave Away
chapters.summary: Quentin and Mireille's POV alternates as they read the letter: their mother traded her own recording career — and the song's copyright — to the radio host who once loved her, in exchange for keeping the family fed and the house in their father's name after he left. The siblings confront how each of them built a life on a lie they half-knew. Climax: Anders arrives mid-argument, and the sale papers are on the table by morning.

chapters.title: Half-Light, Whole Song
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the closing, Quentin asks the question the family arranged itself around — whether the house, like the song, was ever truly their mother's to give away alone. Anders, moved, withdraws his share of the proceeds; Mireille proposes turning the house into a residency for immigrant musicians. Quentin translates her mother's letter into her fading language and finds the words returning. The beat is belonging, chosen rather than inherited.
